name: Still House Plants
label: Bison
lede: Finlay Clark, Jess Hickie-Kallenbach and David Kennedy met at the Glasgow School of Art and started playing in front of a wall of houseplants. Guitar, voice and drums, taken apart and rebuilt as they play, got them from a tenement flat to Pitchfork's Best New Music.

eras.title: Plants in front of the amp
eras.text: Three students at the Glasgow School of Art turn a painting-class friendship into a band that behaves like an art project. Glasgow's Green Door studio and the tape label GLARC give them a first home.

years.src: The Quietus: Hearts Of Glass · Tone Glow
years.h: Clark, Hickie-Kallenbach and Kennedy start at the Glasgow School of Art
years.p: Finlay Clark, Jess Hickie-Kallenbach and David Kennedy all arrive in 2013. Clark and Kennedy share a painting class.
years.xp: The Quietus puts all three in the same year of Glasgow School of Art freshers in 2013, making music together from 2014. In a Tone Glow interview, the band says it began with Clark and Hickie-Kallenbach playing together, with Kennedy joining about a year later.

years.src: The Quietus: Hearts Of Glass · Tone Glow · AllMusic
years.h: The plants go between the band and the room
years.p: At a Glasgow house-exhibition festival, playing as Your Hair Cut, they set their potted plants in front of themselves. The plants stayed and gave the band its new name.
years.xp:
The Quietus places the debut in a tenement flat during Glasgow's Open House festival, surrounded by Kennedy's paintings. Clark told Tone Glow the plants made a barrier between band and audience, and that the name also nods to Still House Group, a New York art collective.

The room filled, with people down the stairs and out into the street, according to the same interview. Silja Strøm, partner of Cafe OTO's Fielding Hope, and Joel White of GLARC were among those in it. Kennedy says they had planned to change the band's name after every show.

years.h: Still House Plants comes out on cassette, on GLARC
years.p: Recorded at Green Door Studio, it is the first release from a trio still at art school. GLARC is a Glasgow tape label that has put out limited cassettes every year since 2016.
years.xp: According to MAP Magazine, the self-titled release was recorded at Green Door Studio while the members were still at art school. GLARC, short for Greater Lanarkshire Auricular Research Council, sold itself as a provider of "cassette based explication" and listening support.

eras.title: Residencies, tours and a collage
eras.text: GLARC puts out a second tape, Bison a debut LP, and Cafe OTO gives them six months in London. A 2019 run through Asia and South America ends with a second LP built from phones and dictaphones.

years.cap: Still House Plants at St John on Bethnal Green, London, June 22, 2017
years.src: Bandcamp: If I don't make it · Wikipedia: Still House Plants
years.h: Assemblages is the last they make in one city until 2024
years.p: The second GLARC release is also the last record all three make in the same city before the 2024 album.
years.xp: The band's Bandcamp notes for the 2024 album say it was made during their first shared city residence since 2017. The Quietus and Wikipedia list Assemblages as a 2017 release on GLARC.

years.h: Bison puts out the first LP, Long Play
years.p: A minimal debut with monochrome artwork, on Bison Records.
years.xp: Exclaim! and AllMusic date the debut to 2018. Wikipedia's list gives 2020, a conflict noted in the file's questions.

years.cap: Clark and Hickie-Kallenbach, with Kennedy on drums, at Servant Jazz Quarters, London, Dec 13, 2018
years.h: A six-month residency at Cafe OTO
years.p: The OTO Projects UK Artists Residency Fund, supported by Jerwood Arts, gives them the slot at the London venue.
years.xp: Cafe OTO's artist page names the residency. Later the band kept rehearsing at the venue's project space, which the Quietus says had been available to them since a residency.

years.cap: Finlay Clark at Servant Jazz Quarters, London, Dec 13, 2018
years.h: A 2019 tour runs through Hong Kong unrest and Santiago protests
years.p: Per Ion Engine, they spend five weeks in Santiago during the protests. The route also takes in Budapest and Buenos Aires.
years.xp: Cafe OTO lists shows at Empty Gallery in Hong Kong, the Hyperlocal festival in Buenos Aires and DIY spaces in Santiago de Chile. The band told Ion Engine it kept an archive of dictaphone and field recordings from these trips.

years.src: Blank Forms · The Quietus: Hearts Of Glass · The Wire
years.h: Fast Edit is stitched together from phones and dictaphones
years.p: The second LP is built from rehearsal, conversation and live recordings of uneven fidelity. Bison released it in Europe and Blank Forms in the Americas.
years.xp:
Blank Forms describes the album as made with "mobile phones, dictaphones, laptop recordings of rehearsals, conversations, and live shows," with "Shy Song" at its center. The Quietus reviewed it as "Hearts Of Glass," hearing guitars that smash and drums that crack, with no samples involved.

The Wire put the band in issue 419. A planned 2020 Counterflows festival slot was cancelled.

eras.title: Back on the road
eras.text: After the pandemic the trio tours Europe, North America, Mexico and Japan, and picks up the attention of the US critics who matter most in 2024.

years.h: Two years of touring, Europe to Japan
years.p: Between 2021 and 2022 the band plays across Europe, North America, Mexico and Japan.

eras.title: If I don't make it, they loved it
eras.text: The album that lands the band on Pitchfork's year-end list was recorded in east London, released on Bison and reviewed almost unanimously well.

years.src: The Quietus: Interview · Wikipedia: If I Don't Make It
years.h: The last record made at Lockdown Studios before it closes
years.p: The band cuts its third album at Lockdown Studios in east London, the final job there before the studio shuts for good.
years.xp:
In the Quietus interview the band describes running instruments through a Leslie cabinet, vocals through DJ software and sidechaining Kennedy's snare to the guitar. "I understood way more about what I wanted from the studio by this record," Kennedy says.

Wikipedia credits Shaun Crook and Darren Clark as producers.

years.src: Bandcamp: If I don't make it · The Quietus: Interview · Wikipedia: If I Don't Make It
years.h: Bison releases If I Don't Make It, I Love U
years.p: Eleven tracks in 46 minutes, opening with "M M M" and ending on the six-minute "More More Faster." It is the band's first record with a colored cover, black and burnt orange.
years.xp: The band had rehearsed the songs for months before recording and said they wanted the record to sound warmer and more rounded. Hickie-Kallenbach says she shared things that felt "honest, real and vulnerable" on this record.

years.src: Wikipedia: If I Don't Make It · Album of the Year · Forced Exposure
years.h: Pitchfork gives it 8.5 and Best New Music
years.p: Jenn Pelly's review says the trio trades song forms for "a kind of collective flickering."
years.xp: The score comes from the album's Wikipedia reception box and albumoftheyear.org. Metacritic's aggregate is 90, marked as universal acclaim. The Guardian called them the most vital band in Britain today, and albumoftheyear.org lists its review as 100.
play: If I Don't Make It, I Love U

years.src: Wikipedia: If I Don't Make It · Album of the Year
years.h: Year-end lists put it 15th at Pitchfork and 4th at Bleep
years.p: Pitchfork places the album 15th on its 50 best of 2024. Exclaim! has it 26th, Uncut 49th and Rough Trade UK 83rd.
years.xp: All placements come from the album's Wikipedia page. Bleep's top ten list had the album fourth.

years.h: A packed, rapt room at London's ICA
years.p: Clash reports a packed and rapturous Institute of Contemporary Arts during release week.
